source: Master Sheet v5.0.0: Islam Haze Wave Cards (16 cards, locked by Jeffrey 2026-11-01) and Haze Anchors (unchanged, already live)

snapshots.label: 600: before Muslim rule
snapshots.title: 600: Before Muslim rule
snapshots.summary: No Muslim state yet exists. Byzantium rules Syria and Egypt, and Persia rules Iraq and Iran.
snapshots.jewish: Jewish communities lived in Babylonia under Persian rule, in the Land of Israel under Byzantine rule, and in Arabia.

snapshots.label: 650: the founding wave
snapshots.title: 650: Arab armies conquer Byzantine and Persian lands
snapshots.summary: Arab armies beat Byzantium at Yarmuk (636) and Persia at Nahavand (639), then took Syria, Egypt and Iraq.
snapshots.jewish: Jewish communities in Babylonia and the Land of Israel came under Arab rule.

spread.text: In conquered Persian lands, some soldiers and elites adopted Islam to retain property or gain military and political roles.

snapshots.label: 700: Umayyad conquests
snapshots.title: 700: Umayyad armies reach Spain, Sindh and Samarkand
snapshots.summary: Umayyad armies took Carthage (697), crossed into Spain (711), conquered Sindh (711) and took Samarkand (712).
snapshots.jewish: Jewish communities in Syria, Iraq and Spain came under Umayyad rule.

spread.text: In early-700s Transoxiana, rulers encouraged conversion with mosques, Persian Quran readings and payments for Friday prayers.

snapshots.label: 800: Abbasids and Sicily
snapshots.title: 800: Abbasid rule and the conquest of Sicily
snapshots.summary: Abbasid caliphs held Baghdad while Aghlabid forces began the conquest of Sicily (827) and took Palermo (831).
snapshots.jewish: Baghdad's Jewish academies and communal self-government grew under Abbasid rule.

spread.text: In Sicily during the 800s–900s, Muslim settlement reshaped towns while religious change in rural areas was slower.

snapshots.label: 900: Fatimid takeovers
snapshots.title: 900: Fatimid and Qarakhanid takeovers
snapshots.summary: Fatimids overthrew the Aghlabids (909) and conquered Egypt (969); Qarakhanids overthrew the Samanids at Bukhara (999).
snapshots.jewish: Jewish communities in Córdoba, Qayrawan and Fustat stayed linked across the rival caliphates.

snapshots.label: 1000: Seljuk conquests
snapshots.title: 1000: Seljuk Turks conquer Iran and Iraq
snapshots.summary: Seljuk Turks beat the Ghaznavids at Dandanqan (1040) and the Byzantines at Manzikert (1071).
snapshots.jewish: Jews in Fatimid Cairo suffered persecution under al-Hakim, then recovered.

spread.text: In Anatolia, conversion and the adoption of Islamic culture transformed society over roughly 1100–1500.

snapshots.label: 1100: Saladin and Ghurids
snapshots.title: 1100: Saladin and the Ghurids expand
snapshots.summary: Saladin took Jerusalem (1187), while the Ghurids conquered Lahore (1186) and Delhi (1192).
snapshots.jewish: Maimonides led Cairo's Jewish community from 1165, and Jews resettled in Jerusalem after 1187.

spread.text: In Delhi, Chishti Sufis helped spread Islam through personal ties and shrine communities in the 1200s–1300s.

snapshots.label: 1200: Khwarazm and Delhi
snapshots.title: 1200: Khwarazmshah and Delhi Sultanate conquests
snapshots.summary: Khwarazmshahs beat the last western Seljuk sultan (1194) and took the Ghurid heartland (1215); Delhi's sultans ruled from 1206.
snapshots.jewish: Almohad rule forced many Jews in Spain and Morocco to convert or flee.

spread.text: In the 1200s, Muslim migrants fleeing Mongol attacks enlarged Delhi’s Muslim community.

snapshots.label: 1300: Mamluks and Timur
snapshots.title: 1300: Mamluk and Timurid conquests
snapshots.summary: Mamluks captured Acre (1291), ending the Crusader states, and Timur took control of Transoxiana (1370).
snapshots.note: In Southeast Asia and West Africa the research records Muslim-ruled port states and kingdoms, such as Pasai and Mali, not conquests.
snapshots.jewish: Jewish settlement revived in Jerusalem and Safed under Mamluk rule.

spread.text: In 1300s Mali, rulers supported Islam by building mosques and encouraging Islamic learning.

snapshots.label: 1400: Timur and the Ottomans
snapshots.title: 1400: Timur's sacks and Ottoman conquests
snapshots.summary: Timur sacked Delhi (1398) and Damascus (1400); Ottomans took Constantinople (1453), Serbia (1459) and Bosnia (1463).
snapshots.jewish: Jews in Mamluk Egypt faced growing restrictions, and exiles from Spain reached Fez.

spread.text: In Bosnia, conversion to Islam was gradual, with its main phase extending from 1463 through the late 1500s.

snapshots.label: 1500: Ottoman conquests
snapshots.title: 1500: Ottoman and Mughal conquests
snapshots.summary: Ottomans took Egypt (1517), Baghdad (1534) and Cyprus (1570); Babur won at Panipat (1526) and founded the Mughal empire.
snapshots.jewish: Jews expelled from Spain in 1492 found refuge in Ottoman lands and North Africa.

spread.text: In Cyprus during 1571–1640, Muslim settlement and local Christian conversions expanded the Muslim population.

snapshots.label: 1600: three empires at war
snapshots.title: 1600: Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal wars
snapshots.summary: Safavids took Baghdad (1623) and Ottomans retook it (1638); Mughals took Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687).
snapshots.jewish: Jews in Safavid Iran faced forced conversion under Abbas II from 1656 to 1662.

spread.text: Around Bijapur, Sufi songs carried Islamic teachings into village households in the 1600s–early 1700s.

snapshots.label: 1700: Nader Shah's conquests
snapshots.title: 1700: Nader Shah takes the throne and Delhi
snapshots.summary: Nader Shah took the Iranian throne (1736) and then Delhi (1739).
snapshots.jewish: Nader Shah moved Jewish families to Mashhad, and Jerusalem's Ashkenazi community collapsed in 1720.

snapshots.label: 1800: Egypt and the Mahdists
snapshots.title: 1800: Egyptian and Mahdist conquests in Sudan
snapshots.summary: Egypt's Muhammad Ali conquered northern Sudan (1820), and the Mahdists captured Khartoum (1885).
snapshots.jewish: Ottoman Jews gained legal equality on paper from 1839, and Damascus Jews faced a blood libel in 1840.

spread.text: In the 1800s, Sufi teachers expanded Islamic religious networks along Sudan’s Nile Valley.

snapshots.label: 1900: Saudi conquests
snapshots.title: 1900: Saudi conquests in Arabia
snapshots.summary: Abdulaziz captured Riyadh (1902) and took eastern Arabia (1913).
snapshots.jewish: Algerian Jews became French citizens in 1870, and Baghdad's Jewish schools modernized from 1864.

snapshots.label: 1920 to 2020: modern states
snapshots.title: 1920 to 2020: new states take shape
snapshots.summary: New states took shape: Turkey (1923), Saudi Arabia (1932), Indonesia (1945), Pakistan (1947) and Algeria (1962).
snapshots.jewish: Most Jewish communities in Muslim lands emigrated between 1948 and the 1970s, mainly to Israel and France.
